instructions: Cut the squid into rings about 1/2 inch wide. Pat them very dry with paper towels. Cut the lemon into wedges. Line a plate with paper towels.
In a medium bowl, whisk 1 1/4 cups of the flour, the baking soda, 1/2 tsp of the salt, the egg and 3/4 cup cold water until it's a thin, smooth batter.
Put the last 1/4 cup flour in a shallow bowl.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F. If you don't have a thermometer, drop in a bit of batter. It's ready when it sizzles right away and floats.
Toss a third of the rings in the flour and shake off the extra. Dip them in the batter, let the extra drip off, and add them to the oil one at a time. Stand back a little. They'll spatter.
Fry for about 2 minutes, turning once, until golden brown. Transfer them to the paper towels and sprinkle with a pinch of the salt.
Fry the rest the same way in two more batches, letting the oil come back to 350°F between them.
Serve right away with the lemon wedges.
method_notes: Fascinating Spain (the lead) coats squid rings in flour, then in a batter of flour, egg, water and baking soda, and fries them in olive oil at 175°C (350°F) in batches, which is what makes them a la romana. Spanish Fiestas flours the squid only and deep fries it for about a minute in sunflower oil. Neither shows a rating, so this is a fallback. The lead's baking soda (1/2 tbsp) was cut to 1/2 tsp as a safer amount. They're gluten containing, as the tags allow.
